subject: B
topic: Important Dates in Indian History/Freedom Struggle

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: In which year did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?
questions.explanation: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919 when General Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful gathering in Amritsar. 1917 is wrong — that was the year of the Champaran Satyagraha. 1920 is wrong — that was when the Non-Cooperation Movement began. 1921 is wrong — that was the year of the Moplah Rebellion.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Quit India Movement:

(i) It was launched in 1942.
(ii) Mahatma Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die' during this movement.
(iii) The movement was launched from Calcutta.
(iv) The British government arrested most Congress leaders immediately after the launch.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942. (ii) is correct — Gandhi gave the famous 'Do or Die' (Karenge ya Marenge) slogan at the Gowalia Tank Maidan. (iv) is correct — British authorities arrested Gandhi, Nehru, Patel, and other Congress leaders within hours of the resolution. (iii) is wrong — the movement was launched from Bombay (now Mumbai) at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, not Calcutta.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The First War of Indian Independence (Revolt of 1857) started from which city?
questions.explanation: The Revolt of 1857 started from Meerut on 10 May 1857 when Indian sepoys refused to use the new Enfield rifle cartridges and mutinied. Delhi is wrong — though the rebels marched to Delhi and captured it, the revolt did not originate there. Kanpur is wrong — Kanpur became a major centre under Nana Sahib but the revolt reached there later. Lucknow is wrong — the siege of Lucknow was a significant event but not the starting point.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885.
Reason (R): A.O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, played a key role in its formation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the INC was founded in December 1885 at Bombay. Reason (R) is also correct — Allan Octavian Hume was instrumental in founding the Congress. However, (R) does not explain WHY the Congress was founded in 1885 specifically; it merely identifies one founder. The founding year was determined by the readiness of Indian political consciousness and the Safety Valve theory, not solely by Hume's involvement. Option 1 is wrong because (R) identifies a founder but doesn't explain the timing. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is factually correct. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is factually correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following events with their years:

Column I:
(a) Partition of Bengal
(b) Rowlatt Act passed
(c) Simon Commission arrived in India
(d) Dandi March

Column II:
(i) 1930
(ii) 1905
(iii) 1928
(iv) 1919

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Partition of Bengal was done by Lord Curzon in 1905 — matches (ii). (b) The Rowlatt Act was passed in 1919 to suppress political activities — matches (iv). (c) The Simon Commission came to India in 1928 — matches (iii). (d) The Dandi March (Salt March) was undertaken by Gandhi in 1930 — matches (i). Option 2 is wrong because it incorrectly assigns Bengal Partition to 1919. Option 3 is wrong because it places the Rowlatt Act in 1928. Option 4 is wrong because it swaps the Simon Commission and Dandi March years.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are events that occurred during the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–1922)?

(i) Boycott of British courts and educational institutions
(ii) Surrender of titles and honours by Indians
(iii) Burning of foreign cloth
(iv) Formation of the Indian National Army

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — boycott of British courts and schools was a key programme of the Non-Cooperation Movement. (ii) is correct — Indians surrendered titles, with Rabindranath Tagore returning his knighthood. (iii) is correct — bonfires of foreign cloth were organized as part of the Swadeshi aspect. (iv) is wrong — the Indian National Army (INA) was formed by Mohan Singh in 1942 during World War II, two decades after the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: India's independence was declared on 15 August 1947 under which Act of the British Parliament?
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 was passed by the British Parliament on 18 July 1947, which provided for the creation of two independent dominions of India and Pakistan on 15 August 1947. The Government of India Act, 1935 is wrong — it provided provincial autonomy but not independence. The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) is wrong — it introduced limited electoral reforms. The Regulating Act, 1773 is wrong — it was the first act to regulate the East India Company's affairs.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Battle of Plassey was fought in the year __________.
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between the British East India Company under Robert Clive and the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah. 1764 is wrong — that was the year of the Battle of Buxar. 1857 is wrong — that was the year of the First War of Independence. 1761 is wrong — that was the year of the Third Battle of Panipat.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Khilafat Movement:

(i) It was started to protest against the British treatment of the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.
(ii) The movement was led by Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali.
(iii) Mahatma Gandhi supported this movement and linked it with the Non-Cooperation Movement.
(iv) The movement was launched in 1930.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Khilafat Movement protested the harsh terms imposed on the Ottoman Empire by the Treaty of Sèvres. (ii) is correct — the Ali brothers (Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali) were the prominent leaders. (iii) is correct — Gandhi supported and merged the Khilafat agitation with his Non-Cooperation Movement to build Hindu-Muslim unity. (iv) is wrong — the Khilafat Movement was launched in 1919–1920, not 1930 (1930 was the year of the Civil Disobedience Movement).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922.
Reason (R): The Chauri Chaura incident, in which a mob set fire to a police station killing 22 policemen, convinced Gandhi that the movement had turned violent.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement on 12 February 1922. Reason (R) is also correct — on 4 February 1922, at Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur, UP), a violent mob burnt down a police station killing 22 policemen. (R) is the correct explanation of (A) because this incident of violence was the direct and stated reason Gandhi gave for calling off the movement, as he believed in strict non-violence. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly caused (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is historically accurate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The famous 'Tryst with Destiny' speech was delivered by Jawaharlal Nehru on which date?
questions.explanation: Nehru delivered the 'Tryst with Destiny' speech on the night of 14 August 1947 (midnight session of the Constituent Assembly), marking India's transition to independence. 15 August 1947 is wrong — though independence was on this date, the speech was given at the midnight session the night before. 26 January 1950 is wrong — that was Republic Day when the Constitution came into effect. 26 November 1949 is wrong — that was the date the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following freedom fighters with the movements they led:

Column I:
(a) Bal Gangadhar Tilak
(b) Subhas Chandra Bose
(c) Bhagat Singh
(d) Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan

Column II:
(i) Khudai Khidmatgar movement
(ii) Home Rule Movement
(iii) Indian National Army
(iv) Hindustan Socialist Republican Association

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Tilak started the Home Rule Movement in 1916 to demand self-governance — matches (ii). (b) Bose reorganized and led the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) — matches (iii). (c) Bhagat Singh was a key member of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) — matches (iv). (d) Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi) founded the Khudai Khidmatgar (Servants of God) movement — matches (i). Option 2 swaps Tilak and Bose. Option 3 swaps Bose and Bhagat Singh. Option 4 swaps Tilak and Bhagat Singh.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 are significant because they:
questions.explanation: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced separate electorates for Muslims, allowing them to elect their own representatives. 'Granted full provincial autonomy' is wrong — provincial autonomy came through the Government of India Act, 1935. 'Abolished the system of dyarchy' is wrong — dyarchy was introduced by the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919) and abolished by the 1935 Act. 'Established universal adult franchise' is wrong — universal adult franchise came only with independent India's Constitution in 1950.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Salt March (Dandi March) of 1930:

(i) It covered a distance of approximately 390 km from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi.
(ii) Gandhi started the march with 78 followers.
(iii) The march began on 12 March 1930.
(iv) The march was a part of the Quit India Movement.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the march covered about 390 km (241 miles) from Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad to Dandi on the Gujarat coast. (ii) is correct — Gandhi started with 78 trusted volunteers from his ashram. (iii) is correct — the march began on 12 March 1930 and reached Dandi on 6 April 1930. (iv) is wrong — the Dandi March was part of the Civil Disobedience Movement, not the Quit India Movement (which was launched in 1942, twelve years later).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly paired as events of 1857?

(i) Revolt at Kanpur led by Nana Sahib
(ii) Revolt at Jhansi led by Rani Laxmibai
(iii) Revolt at Lucknow led by Tatya Tope
(iv) Revolt at Delhi where Bahadur Shah Zafar was declared the Emperor

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Nana Sahib (Dhondu Pant) led the revolt at Kanpur. (ii) is correct — Rani Laxmibai led the revolt at Jhansi. (iv) is correct — Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed the Emperor of India by the sepoys at Delhi. (iii) is wrong — the revolt at Lucknow was led by Begum Hazrat Mahal, not Tatya Tope. Tatya Tope was Nana Sahib's general who operated mainly around Kanpur and central India.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Swadeshi Movement was launched as a protest against:
questions.explanation: The Swadeshi Movement was launched in 1905 as a direct protest against Lord Curzon's Partition of Bengal, which divided Bengal along religious lines. The Rowlatt Act of 1919 is wrong — it led to protests and the Jallianwala Bagh incident, not the Swadeshi Movement. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre is wrong — it was a consequence of anti-Rowlatt agitation. The Simon Commission of 1928 is wrong — it was protested with 'Simon Go Back' slogans, not through a Swadeshi agitation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Cripps Mission of 1942 failed to satisfy Indian leaders.
Reason (R): The Cripps Mission offered only Dominion Status after the war and did not promise immediate independence.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Cripps Mission was rejected by both the Congress and the Muslim League. Reason (R) is also correct — the Mission offered Dominion Status (not full independence) to be granted only after World War II ended. (R) correctly explains (A) because the offer of mere Dominion Status postponed until after the war was the primary reason Indian leaders rejected it — they demanded immediate self-governance. Option 2 is wrong because (R) does explain (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is historically accurate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Poona Pact of 1932 was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and __________.
questions.explanation: The Poona Pact was signed on 24 September 1932 between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, resolving the dispute over separate electorates for depressed classes. Jawaharlal Nehru is wrong — he was not a party to this specific pact. Muhammad Ali Jinnah is wrong — the Poona Pact concerned the depressed classes issue, not Hindu-Muslim matters. Vallabhbhai Patel is wrong — though he was a senior Congress leader, the pact was specifically between Gandhi (who was fasting) and Ambedkar (who represented the depressed classes).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Indian Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950. Why was this particular date chosen?
options: It was the date of India's independence
The Indian National Congress had declared 26 January as 'Purna Swaraj Day' in 1930
It was the birthday of Mahatma Gandhi
It was the date when the Constituent Assembly first met
questions.correctAnswer: The Indian National Congress had declared 26 January as 'Purna Swaraj Day' in 1930
questions.explanation: 26 January was chosen because the Indian National Congress had declared complete independence (Purna Swaraj) on 26 January 1930 at the Lahore session. 'It was the date of India's independence' is wrong — India became independent on 15 August 1947. 'It was the birthday of Mahatma Gandhi' is wrong — Gandhi was born on 2 October. 'It was the date when the Constituent Assembly first met' is wrong — the Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Acts/Reforms with their key provisions:

Column I:
(a) Regulating Act, 1773
(b) Charter Act, 1833
(c) Government of India Act, 1919
(d) Government of India Act, 1935

Column II:
(i) Introduced dyarchy in provinces
(ii) Provided for provincial autonomy
(iii) Established the Supreme Court at Calcutta
(iv) Made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) The Regulating Act, 1773 established the Supreme Court at Calcutta — matches (iii). (b) The Charter Act, 1833 redesignated the Governor-General of Bengal as the Governor-General of India — matches (iv). (c) The Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced dyarchy in provinces — matches (i). (d) The Government of India Act, 1935 introduced provincial autonomy — matches (ii). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (c) and (d). Option 4 incorrectly assigns provisions.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was significant because:
options: It united the Congress and the Muslim League on common political demands
It led to the formation of the Swaraj Party
It resulted in the partition of Bengal being annulled
It established separate electorates for Hindus
questions.correctAnswer: It united the Congress and the Muslim League on common political demands
questions.explanation: The Lucknow Pact (1916) brought the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League together on a common platform, with Congress accepting separate electorates and both demanding self-governance. 'It led to the formation of the Swaraj Party' is wrong — the Swaraj Party was formed in 1923 by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru. 'It resulted in the partition of Bengal being annulled' is wrong — the annulment happened in 1911. 'It established separate electorates for Hindus' is wrong — separate electorates were for Muslims (Morley-Minto Reforms, 1909), not Hindus.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946:

(i) It rejected the demand for a separate Pakistan.
(ii) It proposed a three-tier federal structure.
(iii) It recommended the formation of a Constituent Assembly.
(iv) It was headed by Lord Mountbatten.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Cabinet Mission rejected the demand for a separate sovereign Pakistan. (ii) is correct — it proposed a three-tier structure (Union, Groups of Provinces, Provinces). (iii) is correct — it recommended the formation of a Constituent Assembly to frame India's constitution. (iv) is wrong — the Cabinet Mission was headed by Lord Pethick-Lawrence (Secretary of State for India), with Sir Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander as members. Lord Mountbatten came later as the last Viceroy in 1947.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who among the following was the first Indian to become the President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee (W.C. Bonnerjee) was the first President of the Indian National Congress at its founding session in Bombay in 1885. Dadabhai Naoroji is wrong — he presided over the Congress in 1886 (second session) and later in 1893 and 1906. Surendranath Banerjee is wrong — he presided over the Congress in 1895 and 1902. Badruddin Tyabji is wrong — he was the third president of Congress in 1887.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Revolt of 1857 failed to achieve its objective of overthrowing British rule.
Reason (R): The revolt lacked a common ideology, central leadership, and was limited mainly to northern and central India.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Revolt of 1857 was suppressed by 1858 and British rule continued. Reason (R) is also correct — the revolt had no unified command, no common ideology, and was geographically limited to parts of northern and central India (Madras, Bombay, Bengal largely remained unaffected). (R) explains (A) because these weaknesses (lack of coordination, limited spread, and no central plan) were the primary reasons for its failure. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly explains (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is historically accurate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress (1929) is historically important because:
options: It passed the resolution for Purna Swaraj (complete independence)
It resulted in the formation of the Muslim League
It elected the first woman president of Congress
questions.correctAnswer: It passed the resolution for Purna Swaraj (complete independence)
questions.explanation: The Lahore Session (December 1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, passed the historic resolution demanding Purna Swaraj (complete independence) from British rule. 'It resulted in the formation of the Muslim League' is wrong — the Muslim League was formed in 1906 at Dhaka. 'It approved the partition plan' is wrong — the partition plan was the Mountbatten Plan of June 1947. 'It elected the first woman president of Congress' is wrong — Sarojini Naidu became the first Indian woman president at the Kanpur session in 1925.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are events that took place in 1947?

(i) Mountbatten Plan announced
(ii) Indian Independence Act passed
(iii) Partition of India into India and Pakistan
(iv) First General Elections held in India

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) was announced on 3 June 1947. (ii) is correct — the Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament on 18 July 1947. (iii) is correct — India was partitioned into India and Pakistan on 14–15 August 1947. (iv) is wrong — India's first General Elections were held in 1951–52, not in 1947.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was enacted during the Governor-Generalship of:
questions.explanation: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was passed during the viceroyalty of Lord Lytton to curb the freedom of the Indian language press. Lord Ripon is wrong — he actually repealed the Vernacular Press Act in 1882. Lord Curzon is wrong — his tenure was 1899–1905, associated with the Partition of Bengal. Lord Dalhousie is wrong — his tenure was 1848–1856, associated with the Doctrine of Lapse.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Champaran Satyagraha (1917):

(i) It was Mahatma Gandhi's first major Satyagraha in India.
(ii) It was conducted against the indigo plantation system.
(iii) It took place in the state of Bihar.
(iv) It was directed against the Rowlatt Act.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Champaran (1917) was Gandhi's first civil disobedience movement in India after returning from South Africa. (ii) is correct — it protested the 'tinkathia' system forcing farmers to grow indigo on 3/20th of their land for European planters. (iii) is correct — Champaran is a district in Bihar. (iv) is wrong — the Rowlatt Act was passed in 1919, two years after Champaran; the Champaran movement was specifically about indigo planters' exploitation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Viceroys with events during their tenure:

Column I:
(a) Lord Canning
(b) Lord Ripon
(c) Lord Curzon
(d) Lord Irwin

Column II:
(i) Partition of Bengal (1905)
(ii) First Factory Act (1881)
(iii) Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931)
(iv) Transfer of power from EIC to Crown (1858)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Lord Canning was the last Governor-General of the East India Company and first Viceroy when power transferred to the Crown in 1858 — matches (iv). (b) Lord Ripon's tenure (1880–1884) saw the First Factory Act of 1881 — matches (ii). (c) Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905 — matches (i). (d) Lord Irwin signed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact on 5 March 1931 — matches (iii). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (c) and (d). Option 4 swaps (b) and (c).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Round Table Conferences (1930–1932) were held in:
questions.explanation: All three Round Table Conferences (1930, 1931, 1932) were held in London to discuss constitutional reforms for India. New Delhi is wrong — though it was the capital of British India, the conferences were held in the British capital. Bombay is wrong — it was a major Indian city but not the venue. Calcutta is wrong — the former capital of British India was not the venue for these conferences either.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following table shows major events of the Indian Freedom Struggle and their years:

Formation of INC → 1885
Partition of Bengal → 1905
Jallianwala Bagh → 1919
Quit India Movement → 1942

What is the time gap (in years) between the longest interval and the shortest interval between consecutive events listed?
questions.explanation: The intervals are: 1905–1885 = 20 years, 1919–1905 = 14 years, 1942–1919 = 23 years. The longest interval is 23 years (Jallianwala Bagh to Quit India) and the shortest is 14 years (Partition of Bengal to Jallianwala Bagh). Difference = 23 – 14 = 9 years. 3 is wrong (incorrect calculation). 6 is wrong (possibly 20–14=6, but that's not longest minus shortest). 7 is wrong (incorrect calculation).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Doctrine of Lapse was introduced by:
questions.explanation: The Doctrine of Lapse was introduced by Lord Dalhousie (Governor-General, 1848–1856), under which any Indian state whose ruler died without a natural male heir would be annexed by the British. Lord Wellesley is wrong — he introduced the Subsidiary Alliance system. Lord Cornwallis is wrong — he introduced the Permanent Settlement (1793). Lord Hastings is wrong — he was associated with the abolition of the Pindari system and consolidation of British supremacy.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are associated with the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930–1934)?

(i) Breaking of the salt law
(ii) Boycott of foreign cloth
(iii) Non-payment of taxes
(iv) Formation of parallel governments

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — breaking the salt law (starting with the Dandi March) was the hallmark of the Civil Disobedience Movement. (ii) is correct — boycott of foreign cloth continued as a key element. (iii) is correct — non-payment of taxes (especially land revenue and salt tax) was a primary weapon. (iv) is wrong — formation of parallel governments was a feature of the Quit India Movement (1942), not the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Bengal Gazette, India's first newspaper, was started in 1780 by:
questions.explanation: James Augustus Hickey started the Bengal Gazette (also called Hickey's Gazette) in January 1780, making it the first printed newspaper in India. Raja Ram Mohan Roy is wrong — he started 'Sambad Kaumudi' (1821) and 'Mirat-ul-Akhbar' (1822). Bal Gangadhar Tilak is wrong — he started 'Kesari' and 'Maratha' in 1881. Dadabhai Naoroji is wrong — he was a political leader and economist, not a newspaper founder.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919):

(i) They introduced the system of dyarchy in the provinces.
(ii) They created a bicameral legislature at the centre.
(iii) They granted universal adult franchise.
(iv) They divided provincial subjects into 'Transferred' and 'Reserved'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — dyarchy (dual government) was introduced at the provincial level. (ii) is correct — a bicameral central legislature was created with the Council of State (Upper House) and the Legislative Assembly (Lower House). (iv) is correct — subjects were divided into 'Transferred' (under Indian ministers) and 'Reserved' (under the Governor). (iii) is wrong — universal adult franchise was NOT introduced; voting rights remained restricted by property, education, and tax qualifications.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Indian National Army (INA) trial of 1945 was held at:
questions.explanation: The famous INA trial (court martial of Shah Nawaz Khan, P.K. Sahgal, and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon) was held at the Red Fort in Delhi in November 1945. Calcutta High Court is wrong — though there were protests in Calcutta, the trial was not held there. Bombay High Court is wrong — it was not the venue. Allahabad High Court is wrong — it was not associated with the INA trial.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows freedom movements and the number of arrests made:

Non-Cooperation (1920–22) → 30,000
Civil Disobedience (1930–34) → 90,000
Quit India (1942) → 100,000

The percentage increase in arrests from the Non-Cooperation Movement to the Civil Disobedience Movement was:
questions.explanation: Percentage increase = ((90,000 – 30,000) / 30,000) × 100 = (60,000 / 30,000) × 100 = 200%. 100% is wrong — that would mean arrests doubled to 60,000. 150% is wrong — that would mean arrests reached 75,000. 300% is wrong — that would mean arrests reached 120,000.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Ilbert Bill Controversy of 1883 was related to:
options: The right of Indian judges to try European offenders
The freedom of the vernacular press
The age of consent for marriage
questions.correctAnswer: The right of Indian judges to try European offenders
questions.explanation: The Ilbert Bill (1883) proposed allowing Indian judges and magistrates to try European British subjects in criminal cases, which led to fierce opposition from Europeans in India. 'The freedom of the vernacular press' is wrong — that was related to the Vernacular Press Act, 1878. 'The introduction of local self-government' is wrong — that was Lord Ripon's Resolution on Local Self-Government (1882). 'The age of consent for marriage' is wrong — that was addressed by the Age of Consent Act, 1891.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following slogans with the personalities who gave them:

Column I:
(a) 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'
(b) 'Jai Hind'
(c) 'Inquilab Zindabad'
(d) 'Give me blood and I shall give you freedom'

Column II:
(i) Subhas Chandra Bose
(ii) Bal Gangadhar Tilak
(iii) Bhagat Singh
(iv) Subhas Chandra Bose

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) 'Swaraj is my birthright' was the famous slogan of Bal Gangadhar Tilak — matches (ii). (b) 'Jai Hind' was the greeting and slogan popularized by Subhas Chandra Bose and the INA — matches (i). (c) 'Inquilab Zindabad' (Long Live the Revolution) was used by Bhagat Singh during the Assembly bombing case — matches (iii). (d) 'Give me blood and I shall give you freedom' was Subhas Chandra Bose's call to the INA — matches (iv). Options 2, 3, and 4 incorrectly reassign these well-documented historical attributions.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held at which city in 1885?
questions.explanation: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay (now Mumbai) from 28–31 December 1885, under the presidency of W.C. Bonnerjee. Calcutta is wrong — it hosted the Congress in 1886 (second session). Madras is wrong — it hosted the Congress in 1887 (third session). Allahabad is wrong — it hosted the Congress in 1888 (fourth session).
